Routes: `/goals?state=proposed`. Screens: `ProposedGoal`, `ProposedList`. Requirements: `GOAL-PROPOSED`.

#### What it’s for

Putting a goal in front of its would-be owner, or a leader, without committing them: a goal for someone else, a level above your team, or next quarter’s idea.

#### How to use it

- Propose one from New goal: on Check, answer “Is it under way?” with “Not yet: propose it”, then Propose goal. It gets a key and a page at once. How it’s measured may wait.
- Its page says Proposed above the title, as a word: it has no status shape, no scorecard and no chart. One block says what it would measure and what it would feed. History lists its changes and comments, with no weeks.
- Make it active (its owner or an admin): From starts as this week, whatever was typed when it was proposed, and the line under it reads the plan back with its dates and the day the first check-in is due. A week already past is asked about, here and by the AI assistant. Stages already done are marked at the first check-in. After it, the page is a new goal’s, with “Post the first check-in”, and the toast has Undo. If something an active goal needs is missing, the button is Finish it, which opens Change at it.
- Change it: the same page as any goal, with no reason ever asked, and its type can still change. Withdraw it: it goes to Recently removed for 30 days, with Undo.
- Make it proposed again: an active goal with no check-ins, from its “…” menu (its owner or an admin). It then has no status and nothing is due until it is made active; the message has Undo. Once a goal has a check-in the item isn’t there, and its Change page says to stop it instead.
- In a review’s walk, Propose a new goal saves one with only a name, who will own it (the goal on screen’s owner to start with) and what it will feed. It isn’t on the agenda, and the next session’s Last time says whether its owner has made it active yet.
- On its owner’s Home, under Needs your response, Proposed goals lists one proposed for you by someone else until you open it (“Rhea proposed a goal for you: …”, or “… for you in Developer Productivity fortnightly: …” when it was proposed in a review), and one that has waited 8 weeks or more (“… has been proposed for 9 weeks. Make it active, or withdraw it.”). Open it goes to the goal; Not yet puts the second off for 8 more weeks. One proposed for you a week or more ago, not yet opened, is Home’s lead when nothing else is asked of you first (“Rhea proposed a goal for you”, with Open it).
- Proposed goals are in no count, health line, Needs attention, review agenda, check-in or wrap-up: Goals counts them apart (“· 2 proposed”) and lists them with the State filter, newest first, each with what it would measure. With the filter on, the Board is one column, Proposed, and the Map draws each in its tree with a dashed outline and the word, the goals above it shown for context; opening one goes to its page. Find lists them with the word Proposed.
- A spreadsheet’s Goals sheet has a State column (active or proposed), and the AI assistant’s create_goal and update_goal take state; make_goal_active makes one active. A goal with check-ins can’t go back to proposed: stop it instead.

#### Who can

Anyone can propose a goal, for anyone. Its owner or an admin makes it active. Whoever proposed it may also change or withdraw it while it is proposed. Everyone can comment, ask its owner a question and watch it.

### Changing a goal or its plan

`edit-goal`. Change a goal on one page: what it is, its plan and target, who owns it and where it fits. Once check-ins have started, a plan change needs a reason.

Routes: `/goals/:goalId/edit`. Screens: `GoalEdit`. Requirements: `PLAN-CHANGE`, `REBASELINE`, `HONEST-NUMBERS`, `GOAL-EDIT-PAGE`, `GOAL-DATES`.

#### How to use it

- Open the goal and choose Change this goal, in the “…” menu or at the foot of About this goal.
- It is one page in four sections: What it is (the name, what it measures and the metric that measures it), Plan and target, Who and where (the owner, the team, the level, what it feeds and what it also helps) and More details (how much it moves the goal it feeds, whether it’s a guardrail, and the data source).
- A link can open the page at a section: add #definition, #plan or #owner to the address. Describe it on a goal with no definition opens What it is. Older links that opened one part of the form land on the matching section.
- The owner, the team and the goals are found by typing a name or a key; a goal already under this one is listed but can’t be chosen to feed it.
- Plan and target has the same two rows as a new goal: Baseline with From, Target with To, each week chosen from the list of weeks with their dates. Changing From or To after check-ins have started is a plan change, so it asks why.
- Plan by week shows the numbers week by week; type over any week.
- After check-ins have started, a change to the plan or target asks why, in a sentence: the box appears as soon as the plan differs. Watchers see it flagged, and it is in the goal’s history.
- Numbers follow the same rule as a new goal: never rounded quietly, and odd ones asked about. A target on the worse side of the start for the metric that measures the goal is asked about too (“Lead time for changes is better lower, but the target is above today”), here, in a spreadsheet and through the AI assistant, and your answer is kept in the goal’s History as Checked.
- A question asked while you type is brought into view, and the cursor stays in the field. Save changes waits for the questions: pressed with one still open, it takes you to the first, wherever it is on the page, and the line above the button says where (“Answer the question above, under Target.”). The second answer, such as “No, I’ll change the numbers”, takes you back to the field.
- A target on the other side of the start flips which way is better, so it is never saved quietly: the form says so (“This makes higher better”) and saves once you tick the yes beneath it. A start, target or week’s number far outside the plan it replaces is asked about the same way. The import, Data and the AI assistant ask the same questions.
- The original plan stays on the chart, dotted, and earlier weeks and closed quarters stay judged against the plan of their day. There is no approval step.
- A range can change between At most, At least and Between under Plan and target, as its limit can; Between asks for the lower limit too.
- A goal’s type can’t change once it is active. While it is proposed, Type, under Plan and target, changes it: “It’s proposed, so its type can still change.”

#### One way out

- Save changes stays at the foot of the window wherever you are on the page, and never covers the field you’re typing in.
- Close and keep the draft, top right, is the only other way out. What you typed is kept on this device: open the page again and it says “Restored your unsaved edits”, with Discard them beside it.

#### Who can

The goal’s owner, or an admin.

## Reviews and the year

### Reviews

`reviews`, from the reviews module. A review walks a set of goals together on a cadence, worst and stalest first, and keeps what was said.

Routes: `/reviews`, `/reviews/new`, `/reviews/:reviewId`, `/reviews/:reviewId/edit`, `/reviews/:reviewId/summary`, `/reviews/:reviewId/print`, `/review`, `/goals/:goalId?review=*`. Screens: `Review`, `Inspect`. Requirements: `REVIEW`, `REVIEW-SETUP`, `REVIEW-RUN`, `REVIEW-DECIDE`, `INSPECT-ACT`, `REVIEW-LIST-STATE`, `REVIEW-AGENDA`, `EXCEPTIONS-FIRST`, `REVIEW-SPEAK`.

#### What it’s for

A regular look at the goals that need it, with notes, questions and actions that stick to the goal.

#### Setting one up

- Choose Set up a review on Reviews. Give it a name and a cadence: every 1, 2 or 4 weeks, on a weekday.
- Pick the goals: every goal at a level, a goal and everything feeding it, or single goals, found by typing their name or key. Then the people taking part, found by typing a name or a team (you and your team are suggested).

#### Running it

- Reviews says where each session stands (not started, in progress with how many reviewed, or held, with the date), when it was last held, and how many actions are open. A session under way is listed first. A session not held by its date is outstanding: it says “Outstanding from” its date and how many days past, with the next session beside it, so the two are never mixed up. The review’s page and the bar you walk it with say the same.
- Walking a review, the bar names the goal you’re on among the goals to discuss, and how many of the whole review are reviewed (the goals with nothing flagged count too). The order is fixed when the session starts: reviewing a goal or saving an action never moves one, Continue review picks up at the goal you left, and Previous goal goes back to ones already reviewed. Opening a goal’s walk from its own address keeps the same order.
- Open a review to see its agenda: one line per goal, the ones to discuss first: its status, its name, its number and the gap to plan. The name always has the room; a long gap wraps beside it instead. Goals on track with nothing flagged are marked reviewed together at the end, or walked one at a time instead. Marking them asks first, and the message after it has Undo. While goals to discuss are left, the review carries on; when they’re all that’s left, Finish review marks them and records the session as held.
- The walk opens each goal’s page in turn, under a bar with the review’s name (in full, on two lines if it needs them) and how far through you are. Mark it reviewed, add a note, ask the owner a question, or agree an action with who and when. Reviewed & next moves on.
- A goal off track or at risk asks first: “What happens next, who, by when?” Add the next step (what, who and the week it’s due by; type to find the person: you and your team are suggested first), or choose We accept the risk and say why. Only then can it be marked reviewed. Skip for now leaves it for later in the session.
- A session opens with Last time: what the previous session agreed, who agreed to do it, by when, and whether it’s done. Whoever does it, whoever agreed it, or an admin can mark it done there. Each goal in the walk shows its own. Goals proposed in it are listed after: “Proposed: … Tunde hasn’t made it active yet.”, or the day they did.
- A new goal the room agrees on: choose Propose a new goal in the walk. Give it a name, who will own it and what it will feed. It is saved as proposed, and its owner sets it up and makes it active.
- Finish review says what was decided (each person’s next steps, the risks accepted, the questions still open) before it records the session as held, and its message has Undo. The walk’s last goal finishes the same way.
- Once the session is held, the review’s page leads with what was said, with every goal reviewed. Owners see questions and actions on their goal page and Home. Print or save as PDF makes a copy of the session.

#### Ending one

- End this review, at the foot of its page: it stops showing as due and keeps its notes and actions on each goal and in exports. Its page says Ended, with Reopen. A review that was never held is deleted instead.
- A note said in a review can be removed by whoever said it, or an admin; the goal’s activity then says “Note removed” in its place. A corrected note says edited.

#### Who can

Anyone can set up a review, and everyone can read every review. Only people in a review, or an admin, speak for it: mark goals reviewed, add a note, accept a risk, and ask a question or agree a next step in it, and only about the goals it covers. Anyone can still ask a question or agree a next step on a goal’s own page. Someone not in a review is told who can add them: someone in it, whoever set it up, or an admin, who can change it. Whoever set it up, or an admin, can end it. Whoever said something, or an admin, can correct it.

### The activity log

`activity`. Activity lists every saved change: who made it, when, and each field’s before and after.

Routes: `/activity`. Screens: `Activity`. Requirements: `CHANGE-LOG`, `NOTES`, `NO-LOST-UPDATES`, `IMPORT-UNDO`.

#### How to use it

- Every save is logged: goals, plans, check-ins, comments, review calls, people and the workspace. Drafts are not.
- Filter by who, a goal or its whole tree, team, level, kind of change (check-ins, plans and targets, goal details, reviews, comments, people, imports, via MCP, wrap-ups) and when.
- Search finds the words on a change: who, the goal and its key, what was said and the numbers. A line under it says how many match; the filters on read as words with Remove (see Finding and choosing). Choose who and which goal by typing their name. Show the changes opens the before and after.
- The search and filters are in the link, so a filtered log can be shared, and Back undoes the last choice. Save .csv exports what is shown.
- Every removal is here too: a goal stopped, a person marked as left, a check-in or comment deleted, a view deleted, a watch stopped, and each restore.
- An import or bulk edit has Undo this import on its entry, for whoever made it or an admin. It puts every row back as it was; rows changed since are skipped and listed on the entry that says it was undone. An import over a year old can no longer be undone.
- The app opens with about the last year of changes, plus every comment, ask and import whatever its age. Show older changes, at the end of the list, fetches older ones a page at a time; a goal’s History has the same.

#### Safe saves

If someone else changed the same goal, review or week since you opened it, your save is refused whole, you’re told, and shown the latest. Nothing is half-saved.

### Wrapping up the year, and the next one

`wrap-up`. In the last two weeks of the year, owners wrap up each goal; then an admin starts the next year.

Routes: `/retro`, `/retro/:goalId`. Screens: `Retro`. Requirements: `RETRO`, `YEAR`, `RESULTS`.

#### How to use it

- A year ends on its last day, the Sunday of its last week, whether or not anyone starts the next. From the day after, nothing in it is due, late or out of date: each goal keeps the last status its owner gave, its result is worked out, and its last quarter closes on the numbers there are.
- The wrap-up opens on the Monday of the year’s last two weeks and stays open for four weeks after the year ends, so the last check-ins and the wrap-up can still be done. It stays open once the next year has begun: Home, Wrap up and Cycles show last year’s until it closes.
- Home offers the wrap-up when it opens. For each goal: how it landed (suggested from where it ended), one thing learned, and carry on or stop. About a minute each.
- Wrap up shows everyone which goals are wrapped up, and how.
- An admin starts the next year from its own page, after a read-back of what carries on, finishes and stops (see Starting the next year). A goal that met its target finishes; one its owner stopped stops; the rest carry on from where they ended: number goals from their last number, milestones with what is left. Links to goals that don’t carry on are dropped. Nobody moves into next year until this one’s last day.

#### Who can

- A goal’s owner, or an admin, wraps it up.
- Only admins start the next year.

### Starting the next year

`start-next-year`. An admin sets up next year from the day the wrap-up opens. Nobody moves into it until this year’s last day, and it can be undone until someone uses it.

Routes: `/workspace/cycles/next`. Screens: `StartNext`. Requirements: `CARRY-GOALS`, `RESULTS`.

#### How to use it

- From the day the wrap-up opens, an admin can open Start {next year} from Cycles, Home or the wrap-up. It says how long the next year runs, and that everyone stays in this year until its last day.
- Before anything changes it reads back what will happen to every goal, in four counts that add up to all of them: how many carry on, how many finish because they met their target, how many stop because their owners said so, and how many aren’t wrapped up yet (and of those, which carry on as they are and which finish).
- Then it says what next year starts with: the goals that carry on, each with its key, owner, team, level and metric; the stages not done that come with them; the open next steps and asks, watches and reviews that follow their goals; any goal that loses its “Feeds into” because the goal above it finishes or stops; plans set by hand that become straight lines; and when the first check-ins are due.
- A number goal that carries on starts from its final number in week 1, with the same target, due at the end of next year. Stages not done are spread evenly over next year. A plan that already ran past the year keeps its dates.
- A final number or a wrap-up given after next year was set up still counts: the carried goal follows it until someone checks in on it or changes it. After that, stop it in next year instead.
- Starting it prepares next year. Everyone stays in this year until its last day, so the last check-ins and the wrap-up carry on; next year opens for everyone on its first Monday. Started after this year has ended, it opens at once.
- Cycles then says the next year is ready, when it opens, and offers Undo. Undo works until someone checks in or changes a goal in the new year; after that Cycles says why it can’t.
- Next year can be started only once. Before the wrap-up opens, the page says the day it can be started from.

#### Who can

- Everyone can read the page.
- Only admins start the next year, or undo it.

## Data in and out

### Data

`data`. Every person, goal, check-in, plan and ask as a table you can search, sort, filter, arrange and export, and the home of spreadsheets in and out.

Routes: `/data`. Screens: `DataTables`, `DataFilters`, `DataLayout`. Requirements: `DATA-TABLES`, `TABLE-LAYOUTS`, `ROUND-TRIP`, `ONE-FORMAT`, `SHARED-DOWNLOADS`.

#### How to use it

- Pick a table. Search it (each word you type starts a word in a shown column, as on Goals, and the line under it says so while columns are hidden; a number like 12.5 is one word; a key like G-48 finds its goal, and on Check-ins and Asks that goal’s rows), sort by any heading, and filter by any column under Filters: a value from its list, a number condition, words, or empty. The line under the search counts the rows and says the sort (Remove the sort undoes it), and the filters read as words, each with Remove. The search, the filters and the sort are in the link, so Back and a shared link show the same table.
- Goals are listed in key order (G-1, G-2 … G-124) until you sort. A cell that doesn’t apply to that kind of goal says so: a range goal shows its limit under Target, and a dash with the reason elsewhere.
- Columns chooses what shows. Drag a heading to move a column, or drag its edge to set a width; the keyboard works too. Columns start compact, so more fit on the screen: a long value is cut short, and shows whole in its field and when you point at it.
- Save this layout keeps the columns, widths, search, filters and sort under a name you reopen from Saved layouts. Back to the usual columns resets it.
- Export and Import are where files come and go (when the workspace has Spreadsheets on). Export saves this table as shown, as .xlsx or .csv, with the visible columns in order, filtered and sorted, and says how many rows and columns that is; Everything… opens the one Export, the whole workbook. Import opens the Import page, which has the template (its first sheet, Start here, says what every column needs: Help’s Every column, and what it needs is the same table) and Past imports. The columns that say which record each row is (a goal’s key and ID, a person’s email) are always added, greyed, at the end when the layout hides them, so the file loads back whatever you hid.
- IDs, keys and emails never change by accident: they are shown but not typed into, except a person’s email.

#### Changing data

- Admins type into cells across tables, then Review changes shows each before and after with any problems: Must fix, or a Check to answer there, as on Import. Save applies them together, with the same rules and change log as Import.
- A past check-in can be corrected here; it is logged with its old and new values. Columns the layout hides keep what the check-in says, so a value can be corrected without showing its cause.
- Choices such as Level, Plan, Must stay, Call, Cause and Recovery offer the same words the spreadsheet uses. An owner or a team is found by typing: choose Change in its cell.

#### Who can

Anyone reads the tables. Admins change them; admins can also pin a saved layout for everyone.

### Importing from a spreadsheet

`import`, from the spreadsheets module. Load a workbook, a zip of CSVs or one CSV to add or change people, goals, plan numbers and check-ins, past weeks included, or to stop a goal.

Routes: `/data/import`, `/import`, `/data/import/check`, `/data/import/check/changes`, `/data/import/done/:importId`. Screens: `Import`, `Check`, `CheckClose`, `Large`, `Changes`, `Imported`. Requirements: `BULK-IMPORT`, `WORKSPACES`, `HONEST-NUMBERS`, `ONE-FORMAT`, `ROUND-TRIP`, `IMPORT-ACTIONS`, `SPREADSHEETS-ON-DATA`, `IMPORT-LEVELS`, `IMPORT-PREVIEW`, `IMPORT-LARGE`.

#### How to use it

- On Data, choose Import, beside Export. Export everything first to start from what is already in the app, or download the template from the Import page to start from nothing.
- Drop a file or choose one (up to 30,000 rows or 20 MB a file, and 5,000 changes at a time; up to 5,000 rows is checked in a second or two). Or choose “or paste rows from a spreadsheet”, paste the cells straight from Excel or Sheets with their header row, then Check these rows. Copy the Goals headers puts the columns you fill in on the clipboard.
- What a new row must have is on the Import page and in Every column, and what it needs: a goal needs Goal, and Owner or Owner email. A number goal also needs Start and Target; a range goal, Limit; a stages goal, Stages. A check-in, Goal key (or Goal), Week, and Value or Stages. A person, Name and Email.
- Change it in Excel, then drop it in or choose the file: an .xlsx workbook, a .zip of CSVs, or one .csv or tab-separated file. Anything Export these goals or Data saves loads back.
- A title row above the headers is fine: the header row is found in the first ten rows, and the preview says which row it was. A column under another name is read as the column it means (Goal name is Goal, Units is Unit); one a letter out (Targett) is asked about once, and so are two columns that mean the same one (Goal and Goal name): you choose which is read.
- Each sheet is known by its header row, whatever the file or sheet is called. Start here (or the README of an older file), Results, Asks, Notes and Metrics are for reading, and left out. So are rows whose Action says Example, such as the template’s: the preview, Data’s review and the AI assistant count them.
- Rows find their goal by its key, then its ID, so a file from last cycle still finds the goals carried over. People are found by email, then by a name only one person has; the preview notes when a name was used.
- To build a whole tree in one file, give each new goal’s row a Ref of your own (top, a1, anything, each row its own). Another row then names it in Feeds into ref, and a check-in in Goal ref, before it has a key. Refs belong to the file: they are never kept, and an export leaves them empty.
- Every column you can change counts: a change to any of them is applied, or shown as a problem. Worked-out columns (Status, Gap, Calculated…) are ignored.
- The Action column: Stop a goal with check-ins (say why in Reason), Delete one set up by mistake, or mark someone as Left (their goals and asks go to Takes over: an email, or a name only one person has). The same rules as the app apply, and the preview shows what each does.
- Every row is checked with the app’s own rules, and Check this import shows the result before anything is saved: the file and what was read (sheets and columns it didn’t read are named), counts by sheet, then what must be fixed, then questions, then what will be saved. Show the changes lists every change in the file’s order, 50 at a time, with each field before and after and how a value Faro supplied was worked out (“the owner’s team; the row gave none”).
- Plan changes after check-ins need a reason. A plan change that flips which way is better, or puts a number far outside the old plan, is a question, and saves only once you say yes.
- To leave without saving, use Close without saving at the top of Check this import or its list of changes: the file is forgotten and you are back on Import. If you answered a question or gave a reason, it asks first.
- A file that changes nothing says Nothing would change. If it edits worked-out cells, such as Status, it says so: Faro never reads them, so to change where a goal stands, post a check-in.
- A file exported from another workspace is asked about first: its keys and IDs belong there, so its rows can be added as new goals, or not at all.
- A number goal’s weeks are From and To, written as a year and a week (2026-W46, 2027-W13). Plan from week and Due week, counted from the cycle’s start, are still written and still load: where a row has both, the one you changed counts, and two that disagree are Must fix; a Due week left empty beside a To says nothing. In a file with no Start column, a bare number under From (“52”) is Must fix: it may be the starting number, so put that under Start, or write the week as 2026-W46. A week a year doesn’t have says so (“2027 has 52 weeks. Use 2027-W52, or 2028-W01.”). A stage may be written Design@48 or Design@2026-W48.
- Past weeks are marked as loaded later, so history never looks like a fresh update. Rows that change nothing are left alone, and so are a stopped goal’s rows.
- Saving ends on Imported: how many rows were saved from which file (counted as Undo counts them), what they were, and the rows left out to download. See the goals, or Undo this import.
- Loaded the wrong file? Undo this import, on Imported, on Data under Past imports, or on its entry in Activity, puts every row back as it was, stopped goals and people who left included. It says first which rows have changed since and will stay.

#### Must fix, and Check

- Must fix is what Faro can’t record as it is: a required column left empty, a word a column doesn’t know (a level of “vp”), text where a number goes, a key used twice, an owner who isn’t here. Nothing saves while one is left; fix it in the file and choose it again.
- Check is a question about something possible but unlikely: a name one letter out (“Did you mean Platform?”), a number with no unit, a stage already past, a target a hundred times its start, a goal with a name its team already uses. Answer it on the page, and it saves.
- The same problem on many rows is said once, with how many rows and where, and one answer covers them all: fourteen rows naming “Platfrom” are one question.
- A name or word one letter out is always asked about, never guessed and never quietly refused. Case, accents, “&” for “and” and punctuation don’t count, so “ci cd” is CI/CD.
- Some answers leave rows out (“Leave these rows out”): those rows aren’t saved, and the rest are.
- Fix the rows in the file: Download the rows to fix gives just those rows, each with a Problem column saying what is wrong. Choose the corrected file and your answers still apply.
- Or leave them out and save the rest: the sheet says which rows go, and the rows that go with them (a new goal’s check-ins, goals that feed into it). Put them back changes your mind.
- An answered question closes to what was asked and your answer, with Change. The focus moves to the next open question, or to the answer just given.
- A person chosen for one owner cell (Choose a person) also stands for the row’s other owner cells that name no one here; a cell that names someone else here, or an Owner ID that can’t be read, is still Must fix.
- An admin answering a team that isn’t here may add it as a new team. A new goal with no Type is read from the columns it fills in: Start and Target a number goal, Limit a range, Stages a stages goal.

#### Large files

- A large file is checked without stopping the page: after a moment, Reading {file} says how far the check has got and what it has found so far. You can keep using Faro in another tab; nothing is saved until you say so. Stop ends the check, and nothing is saved.
- The changes, and a question’s rows, are shown 50 at a time, with Show 50 more.
- Faro saves up to 5,000 changes in one import. A file that would change more is checked, not saved: Download as {k} files of 5,000 rows splits it, keeping each goal with its plan and check-ins and a goal before the goals that feed into it. Import the parts in order; each has its own Undo.

#### Who can

Owners change their own goals; admins can change any, and add and change people. Rows for other people’s goals are fine if you leave them as they are.

### Exporting

`export`, from the spreadsheets module. One button: Export .xlsx. Zipped CSVs, one sheet as CSV, JSON and a brief for an AI chat are under Other formats.

Screens: `Export`, `ExportButton`, `DataMenu`. Requirements: `EXPORT`, `SHARED-DOWNLOADS`, `ONE-FORMAT`.

#### How to use it

- On Goals, choose Export these goals. When the goals are filtered, it starts from the ones shown now; Everything in the cycle is one click away, with how many goals, check-ins and people that is: stopped and proposed goals count, as the workbook holds them.
- Export .xlsx is the one button. The file’s name is at the foot of the sheet before you press it, with how many goals it holds as of this week, and the message after says it again: Exported platform-goals-all-2026-11-05.xlsx. Import’s Download the workbook saves the same file, by the same name.
- A view that shows no goals has nothing of its own to export: the sheet starts from everything, and None shown now can’t be chosen. On Data, a table that shows no rows says so instead of saving a file of headers.
- On Data, Export saves the open table exactly as laid out, as .xlsx or .csv, with the columns that say which record each row is added so it loads back; the menu says how many rows and columns that is. Everything… opens the same Export as Goals. Import is beside it.
- Excel workbook, the usual choice: a first sheet, Start here, that says for every column what it means, whether a new row must have it, its format and an example; then Goals, Plan, Check-ins, People, Results (each goal’s result and its quarters, for year-end reporting), Asks, Notes and Metrics. Worked-out columns are in grey. A goal stopped this year is in it, with Stopped as its status.
- Other formats: CSV files, zipped (the same sheets, one CSV each with the same headers); one sheet as CSV, chosen in its row; JSON; and the brief for an AI chat.
- The template is on the Import page and in Every column, and what it needs: Start here, then Goals, Plan, Check-ins and People with only the columns you fill in. The headers a new row must have are in bold, and the example rows say Example in Action, so they are never imported. It is saved as faro-template.xlsx.
- One format: whatever you export can be edited and loaded back on Data’s Import, or used to set up a new workspace. Loaded back unedited, it changes nothing. Each person is written with their name and email.
- JSON: everything, with each goal’s plan and check-ins inside it, in a stated format.
- Brief for an AI chat: Markdown that leads with decisions waiting on people, then each goal’s story, then results. Copy it or save it.
- Every file the app saves, here and elsewhere, is named the same way: the workspace, what it holds, which goals, and the date. Which goals is all (only ever for everything), the view’s name, or as-shown for a table from Data or a filtered All tab: platform-goals-all-2026-11-05.xlsx, platform-goals-off-track-2026-11-05.xlsx, platform-check-ins-as-shown-2026-11-05.csv.
- Exports hold names and the owners’ reasons. Share them as you would the app.

### Every column, and what it needs

`columns`, from the spreadsheets module. For every column of Goals, Plan, Check-ins and People: whether a new row must have it, its format, an example, and what happens when it’s left empty.

Screens: `ColumnsHelp`. Requirements: `FIELD-TABLE`, `ONE-FORMAT`.

#### What it’s for

The same table is the first sheet of the template and of every workbook, Start here, and docs/export-format.md is made from it too, so none of them can disagree.

#### What the words mean

- Required: a new row can’t be saved without it. Owner or Owner email: one of the two is enough.
- Required for a number goal (or a range or stages goal): required when the goal is of that type, such as Target for a number goal. Required when…: in that situation only, such as Cause when a check-in is behind plan.
- Optional: it can be left out; the table says what an empty cell gives.
- Leave empty: Faro fills it in, such as a new goal’s Key.
- Worked out: Faro writes it and never reads it back, such as Status. Leave it or delete it.
- On a row already here, nothing is required: an empty cell keeps what is there, except where the table says empty clears it. So an empty Admin keeps an admin an admin; type no to take it away.
- State on Goals says active or proposed. proposed adds a goal that is proposed, not yet active (its Start and Target, Limit or Stages may wait), or makes one with no check-ins proposed again; active makes a proposed goal active, once it has everything an active goal needs. A proposed goal’s worked-out columns are empty, and its Status says Proposed. A check-in row for a proposed goal is a Must fix.

### Past imports and Undo

`past-imports`, from the spreadsheets module. Every import, bulk edit and change through MCP in one list, newest first, each with who made it, how, what it changed, and Undo.

Routes: `/data/imports`. Screens: `PastImports`. Requirements: `IMPORT-UNDO`, `CHANGE-LOG`.

#### The list

- On Data, choose Import, then the link to past imports at the foot of the page. Each line is one import: the file’s name (or Bulk edit on Data, Bulk edit on Goals, Changes through MCP), who made it, when, how, and what it changed.
- Find one by its file, by who made it or by what it changed; a search that finds nothing says so. Open one to see what it saved.
- In Activity an import is one entry too, with its rows folded under it: Show the changes lists them. Search still finds each row, and each goal’s history still shows its own.

#### What Undo puts back

- Undo puts every row the import wrote back as it was: a goal or check-in it added is deleted, one it changed gets its earlier version back, a goal it stopped is live again, someone it marked as left comes back, and a team it added or changed goes back too.
- A goal that fed one Undo deletes moves up to what that goal fed. Someone the import added stays while they lead a team, sit in a review or have an ask.
- Before anything is undone, it says how many rows go back and which stay as they are because they changed after the import, each with why: “Rhea Kapoor posted a check-in for week 45 on 12 Nov”, “Its target was changed on 10 Nov”.
- When every row has changed since, there is nothing left to undo, and it says so.
- Two imports of the same rows can be undone newest first: once the newer one is undone, the older one puts back everything it wrote.
- Once undone, the line says when and by whom, and Undo is gone.

#### Who can

Whoever made the import, or an admin. Everyone else sees the list without Undo.

### Printing a goal or a review

`print`. A goal or a review session on one clean page, ready to print or save as a PDF.

Routes: `/goals/:goalId/print`. Screens: `Print`. Requirements: `PRINT-EXPORT`.

#### How to use it

- On a goal’s page or a review, choose Print or save as PDF.
- A goal prints on one A4 page: status, the number against plan and target, the facts, chart, path to green, latest check-in, requests, the three latest review notes, quarters and contributing goals. The reason is printed once, under Why.
- A review prints its session worst first, with what was said.
- Print uses black on white with the status shapes kept, and no navigation.

## People, workspace and settings

### Removing, stopping and undoing

`removing`. Anything you make can be taken away again: people leave, goals stop, check-ins, reviews, comments and views go, an import can be undone, and nothing is ever lost.

Routes: `/workspace/removed`. Requirements: `REMOVE-ANYTHING`, `UNDO-REMOVE`, `PERSON-LEFT`, `GOAL-STOP`, `IMPORT-UNDO`.

#### What it’s for

Mistakes and changes of plan. A person leaves, a goal stops mattering mid-year, a check-in went to the wrong goal, a spreadsheet loaded the wrong numbers. Each can be put right without losing history.

#### What each removal does

- A person who has left: an admin opens them on Workspace, under People, and chooses Mark as left. The dialog first asks who takes over their goals and their open asks (the ones they raised and the ones waiting on them). They then disappear from pickers, counts, reviews and Home, and their MCP token stops working. Everything they did keeps their name, as “Maya Patel (left)”. Someone with no goals, check-ins, notes or asks is deleted instead.
- A goal with check-ins is stopped, with a reason (“…” menu → Stop this goal). It leaves the numbers, reviews, Home, Watching and the lists of what needs attention, but its page stays, marked Stopped with its reason, and so do its history, its place in exports and Activity. The goals feeding it now feed what it fed; its open asks are withdrawn with a note. A goal with no check-ins is deleted instead.
- A check-in: Delete this check-in, under the latest one on the goal’s page, by the goal’s owner. Undoing an import puts a check-in back only for someone who may check in on that goal: an admin can undo a workbook they loaded, but not an owner’s own correction. Once a newer one is posted it can only be corrected. The status goes back to the one before.
- A review: End this review, at the foot of its page, by whoever set it up or an admin. It keeps its notes and actions and stops showing as due. One that was never held is deleted.
- A comment: its author can edit it (it then says edited), and its author or an admin can remove it; its place in the thread says “Comment removed”, so the conversation still reads. A note said in a review works the same way, leaving “Note removed”.
- A saved view: Delete, from its menu. An admin can delete anyone’s. Stopping watching works the same way.
- A cycle no one has checked in to yet (started by mistake, say): an admin deletes it under Cycles on Workspace, with its goals.
- An import or bulk edit: Undo this import, on its entry in Activity, by whoever made it or an admin. Every row it wrote goes back as it was: goals and check-ins it added are deleted, ones it changed get their earlier version back. A row someone has changed since is skipped and listed.

#### Undo, and Recently removed

- Every removal shows a message with Undo for 10 seconds. Undo puts everything back as it was a moment before, including what was handed over or moved.
- After that, Recently removed on Workspace brings things back: it lists what was removed, stopped, ended or marked as left in the last 30 days, with who did it and when, and Restore. An admin sees everything; anyone else sees what they removed themselves, and can restore it.
- Nothing is ever erased. After 30 days a removed record leaves the list, but it’s still kept, and every removal and restore is in Activity.

#### Who can

- Admins mark people as left, delete people with no history, delete cycles and restore anything from Recently removed; anyone restores what they removed.
- A goal’s owner or an admin stops or deletes it. Whoever posted a check-in, or an admin, deletes it. Whoever set up a review, or an admin, ends it.
- Only a comment’s author edits it; its author or an admin removes it. Whoever made an import, or an admin, undoes it.
- Through MCP, an AI tool can do each of these with the same rules, as the person whose MCP token it uses.

### Workspace: about this one

`workspace`. Workspace opens on About: for admins, what needs sorting out; then the facts about this workspace, each leading to its section. Its other sections are Cycles, Privacy and Recently removed for everyone, and Access and Features for admins.

Routes: `/workspace`, `/workspace/overview`. Screens: `Workspace`. Requirements: `ADMIN`, `WORKSPACE-ADMIN`, `WORKSPACES`, `WORKSPACE-SECTIONS`, `WORKSPACE-ABOUT`, `WORKSPACE-ONE-PLACE`.

#### About

- Under Workspace’s title, one line says whose workspace it is and your part in it: “Platform Engineering · you’re an admin here”, or a member.
- For admins, first, To sort out: no goals yet in the year, no review set up, being the only admin of five people or more, people with no email, people in no team, and teams of three or more with no lead. Each says why it matters and has one button that leads to where it’s dealt with. Three show at a time; “and 2 more” shows the rest. When there is nothing, the block isn’t there at all.
- Then the facts: its name (the example’s says “example data”; one you made in the demo, “kept in this browser”), how many people in how many teams (leading to People), the year and when its wrap-up opens (leading to Cycles), who the admins are (leading to Access, for admins; anyone else is told to ask one of them), which optional features are on (leading to Features) and whether how the app is used is recorded (leading to Privacy).
- Admins rename the workspace with Rename, beside About this workspace. A name has at most 80 characters, and the field counts them as you near the limit.
- Admins of a workspace of their own (not the example) can delete it at the foot of About, after typing its name. It can’t be undone. The example is put back as it was with Start over, in Demo controls, which only touches this browser.

#### Switching, and setting one up

- The workspace’s name at the top of the sidebar (on a phone, the line under the page’s name at the top) is the workspace switcher. It lists every workspace you can open with what kind it is; the open one says Open now and your role. Under the list: About, which opens Workspace, and Set up a new workspace. It says Switch beside its arrow.
- Land in another workspace as someone else, or with another role, and one line says so: “You’re Rhea Kapoor here, a member.” A workspace you can’t open yet still lists the others, to open one of them.
- A workspace is one organisation’s goals and the people who share them: its own people and teams, its own goal year and check-in day, and its own admins. About says so, under its name.
- Switching is a page move: Back takes you to the workspace you came from. You land on the same page in the other workspace when it has one (Home, Goals, Reviews, People, a Workspace section), otherwise on Home; from a person’s or a team’s page, on People or Teams. While it opens, the page says so.
- Part-way through a check-in, a new goal or a review, switching asks first: what you’ve typed stays as a draft in its own workspace, in this browser, for when you switch back.
- Switch person (your name at the foot of the sidebar) is only about people. Where you’re an admin, it says Admin.

#### Finding your way

- On a computer, the sections are in a menu down the left, About first. On a phone, Workspace is About, and the other sections follow under More in Workspace, each with one line; a section opens with Workspace at the top to go back.
- Each section has its own address, so you can bookmark one or send a link to it: /workspace/cycles, /workspace/privacy and so on. /workspace/overview, and older links from a GitHub issue, still open the page they meant.
- People and Teams moved out of Workspace to People, in the sidebar, for everyone. See People: finding someone, and Teams.
- Cycles: the goal years, for everyone to read; only admins delete one. Privacy: what the app records, for everyone to read; only admins switch it. Recently removed: an admin sees everything removed lately, anyone else what they removed. Access (the admins and MCP access) and Features: for admins. Each has its own article.

#### Leaving

- Leaving a workspace is in Settings, at the end: someone takes over your goals and open asks first, then you’re gone from its pickers, counts, reviews and Home; your history stays, under “Name (left)”, and an admin can bring you back from Recently removed for 30 days.
- The only admin can’t leave until someone else is an admin.

#### Who can

- Everyone sees About, Cycles, Privacy and Recently removed (their own removals). Someone who isn’t an admin and opens Access or Features is told who the admins are, with a way back to Workspace.
- Only admins add or change people and teams, mark people as left, restore what was removed, make tokens, turn recording or features on or off, rename or delete the workspace. Whoever sets up a workspace is its first admin. In the demo, Start over (in Demo controls) is for everyone: it only touches this browser.
- Feedback, the inbox of markups and feedback, is its own page beside Help, open to anyone. See The inbox.

#### For the people building Faro

- Sections are an extension point: a feature module adds its own with `sections` in its app.tsx and module.json, and it appears in the menu, at /workspace/<id>, for as long as the module is on. A section can give a fact for About (`says`) and its own things to sort out (`needs`).

### People: finding someone

`people`. Everyone in the workspace, A to Z: find someone by name, job title or team, open them to see their team, their goals and their reviews. Admins add and change people.

Routes: `/people`, `/people/:personId`, `/workspace/people`. Screens: `People`. Requirements: `PEOPLE-DIRECTORY`, `OLD-ADDRESSES`, `PROFILES`, `PERSON-LEFT`, `PERSON-EMAIL`, `SAME-NAMES`.

#### What it’s for

People is in the sidebar (on a phone, under More), for everyone. It answers who someone is, what team they are in, and how their goals stand.

#### How to use it

- Type in the search to find someone: each word you type starts a word of their name, job title or team, so “eng man” finds the Engineering Managers. Capitals and accents don’t matter: “lucia” finds Lucía.
- Filter by a team (its lead counts as one of its people), or tick Admins only. On a phone both are under Filter.
- The list is A to Z (with a search, those whose name starts with it first), 50 at a time; the line under the search says how many, and Next and Previous turn the pages. The search and filters are in the address, so Back and a shared link bring the same list back.
- Each row says the person’s job title and team, and beside it whether they are an admin, which team they lead and how many goals they own this year.
- Open someone to see their page: their team (and any other team they lead), their email, whether they are an admin, their goals counted by status (each count opens those goals) and the reviews they run or are in. See their goals opens Goals for just them.

#### For admins

- Add a person is the page’s main action; the new person’s page opens once they are added. Everyone new needs an email, and no two people share one.
- When some people have no email yet, a line above the list says how many, with Add them: type the emails you know and save them together.
- On a person’s page, under For admins: Change details (name, email, job title and team), Make an admin or Remove as admin (there is always at least one admin), Make an MCP token in the real app, and, apart, Mark as left (on your own page: to leave, use Settings). Marking someone as left asks who takes over their goals and open asks first; history keeps their name as “Name (left)”. Someone with no history is deleted instead.
- Two people can have the same name: the email is who someone is, and wherever both could be on screen each shows their team or job title beside the name.

#### Who can

Everyone sees People, Teams and every person’s and team’s page. Only admins see the buttons that change them.

#### Moved

People used to be a section of Workspace. Its old address, /workspace/people, still opens it.

### Metrics: what each number means

`metrics`, from the metrics module. The metric library: each number goals are measured by, defined once, with its page saying what it means and every goal measured by it, side by side.

Routes: `/metrics`, `/metrics/:metricId`, `/data/metrics`. Screens: `Metrics`, `MetricPlaces`. Requirements: `METRICS-LIBRARY`.

#### What it’s for

A metric says exactly what a number means (what is counted, over what, its unit and which way is better), so two teams’ “build time” mean the same thing. Metrics is in the menu after People (on a phone, under More), for everyone.

#### How to use it

- The library lists every metric A to Z, 50 a page. Each row says its unit, which way is better and who owns it, and its goals by status, worst first, or “No goals yet”.
- Find a metric by its name, unit, owner or meaning: “min lower” finds those in minutes where lower is better. Unit and Used by narrow the list beside the search; Filters has Owner, Which way is better, No goals use it and Something to sort out. Sort by A to Z, Most goals first or Changed lately. The filter line says what is on, each with Remove.
- A search that finds nothing offers to add it as a new metric.
- Open a metric to see what it means and how it’s calculated, then every goal measured by it as a table: its status as a shape and a word, the goal, who it is for (a team, or the whole company), the latest number, the target with its week, and where it stands against plan (for a goal kept in range, its room to the limit). When two or more goals have a number, a line says the lowest and highest now.
- A proposed goal that names the metric is listed under the table, apart, as “Proposed · 1”: its name, key and owner, with no numbers. It is in no comparison until it is made active.
- Below them: where the number comes from, who owns that source, how often it refreshes, any caveats, and who added and last changed it. With one goal, See its goal opens it.
- On a goal measured by a metric, its summary says “Measured by …”, and its page has a block with the metric’s meaning and a link to the other goals measured by it. A person’s page lists the metrics they own, and a team’s the metrics its goals use.
- Old links to Metrics under Data still work: they open the library, a metric, or the form.

#### Who can

- Anyone reads the library and every metric, and anyone adds a metric.
- A metric’s owner and admins change or remove it. They also see what it still needs (an owner, a meaning, a source, a goal that uses it) on its page, under To sort out, and as a warning on its row in the library. Everyone else sees who can change it.

### Defining a metric well

`metric-define`, from the metrics module. A metric needs three things to be used: a name, a unit and which way is better. The rest can be said later, and its page says what is still to say, in words, never as a score.

Routes: `/metrics/new`, `/metrics/:metricId/edit`. Requirements: `METRIC-DEFINED`, `METRICS-CARE`.

#### What it needs

- In Metrics, choose Add a metric. Three things are needed: the Name (3 to 120 characters, used by one metric whatever the case or accents), the Unit as it follows a number (hours, %, USD, deploys), and Which way is better. Decimal places is optional: 0 if left.
- Five more make it fully defined, and can be said later: what it means and how it’s calculated (what is counted, out of what or over what period, and what is left out); where the number comes from; who owns that source; how often it refreshes; and an owner here who answers for what it means.
- A metric’s page says “Fully defined” under its title, or what is still to say: “Still to say: where the number comes from, how often it refreshes.” Its owner and admins can open the form at each item from there. It is never a score, a percentage or a bar, and nothing is sorted by it.

#### Must fix and Check

- A Must fix stops the save until it is fixed: a name missing, too short or already used, no unit, or no direction. It shows under its field, outlined, once you leave the field or try to save.
- A Check is a question to answer once. There are three: a name one letter or one word from another metric’s, or one a metric used to have (“This is one letter from “Deploy success rate” …”, with Use that one or Mine is different: keep it); a unit spelt differently from one in use (“Other metrics here use “min”.”); and a percentage whose meaning doesn’t say out of what (with It’s right as written).
- The foot of the form counts them (“1 to fix, 2 to check.”) above the completeness line. Saving with a Check unanswered takes you to it. An answered Check closes to one line with Change; changing the field asks again.
- Use that one opens the metric already in the library; what you typed is kept as a draft.
- Adding a metric from a goal’s Measured by asks the same Checks, under the new metric’s fields, before Add this metric saves it.

#### Changing or removing one

- What you type is kept as a draft: Close, Back or a reload doesn’t lose it. Opened from a metric’s To sort out or its completeness line, the form opens at the field that needs filling.
- Changing the unit or which way is better of a metric goals use asks first, here and through the AI assistant: their numbers and plans don’t change, and the goals that now differ say so under “Measured by” on their page.
- Workspace → About tells admins how many metrics have no owner (someone who left owned them), with See them.
- On a metric’s page, its owner and admins choose Change this metric, or Remove this metric. Removing one stops its goals being measured by it (they keep their numbers and plans); Undo, or Recently removed for 30 days, puts it back.
- An AI assistant asks the same questions: save_metric returns them and saves nothing until it calls again with your answers to those questions. Someone who may not change a metric is told so before being asked anything.

### Measured by: choosing a goal’s metric

`metric-measured-by`, from the metrics module. In New goal and when changing a goal, say which metric measures it by typing to find one, or add one there.

Screens: `MeasuredBy`. Requirements: `METRICS-MEASURED-BY`.

#### How to use it

- In New goal, “Measured by” is the first field on the step about numbers; when changing a goal, it is under its name. Type part of a metric’s name, unit or owner to find it. Metrics already in the goal’s unit are offered first.
- Choosing one shows what it means, with Read more for its page. On a new goal whose unit nobody has typed, it fills in the unit, the decimal places and which way is better, said in one line; Use different ones shows the fields again.
- For: the goal’s team, or the whole company. With no team chosen yet, only the whole company is offered. Which part narrows it to one part of that number; see “Measured by: for whom, and which part”.
- A goal in another unit can’t be measured by the metric: it says so, and the goal can’t be saved until the units agree or No metric is chosen.
- No metric means the goal says in its own words how it’s measured. A goal with dated stages has no number, so it has no “Measured by”.
- Nothing fits? Choose Add “…” as a new metric: give it a name, a unit and which way is better, and it is chosen. You own it; say more about it on its page later.
- Check reads it back (“Measured by …, for …”). On Goals, Filters has Measured by, and a metric’s page has See its goals.

### Measured by: for whom, and which part

`metric-slices`, from the metrics module. What a goal takes from its metric and what stays its own, whose number it is, and one part of that number.

Requirements: `METRIC-PARTS`.

#### What a goal takes from its metric

- A goal measured by a metric uses the metric’s unit and which way is better, shown as “From the metric”, with where the number comes from and how often it refreshes when the metric says. To use others, choose another metric or No metric.
- Its start, target, plan and due week stay the goal’s own.

#### For, and which part

- For says whose number it is: the goal’s team, or the whole company.
- Which part is optional: one part of that number, such as tier-1 services, a region or release builds, up to 60 characters. Leave it empty for all of it.
- Parts other goals on the metric already use are listed under the field; choose one rather than typing it again, so goals on the same part line up on the metric’s page. A part spelt like one in use is asked about (“Use tier-1 services”, or keep yours).
- If another goal already measures the same metric for the same team and part, you are asked, as two goals on one number is unusual; Carry on keeps it.

#### After check-ins

- Once a goal has check-ins, changing its metric, For or part asks Why. It shows in the goal’s History, so anyone reading its chart knows the number was measured differently from then on.

#### On the goal’s page

- About lists Measured by: For, what it means, From the metric, where the number comes from, caveats, the goal’s own target, and its own definition when that says more than the metric’s.

### Changing, retiring and merging a metric

`metric-change`, from the metrics module. Which changes save at once, the ones that tell a metric’s goals first, and retiring, bringing back and merging.

Routes: `/metrics/:metricId/edit`. Requirements: `METRIC-CHANGE`.

#### What saves at once

- A new name, owner, source owner, refresh or caveats saves at once, as does any change to a metric no goal uses.

#### What reads back first

- Changing what a metric means, or where its number comes from, shows the goals it measures and asks “Is it still the same number?”. Same number, better words: nothing is marked. The number itself changes: say why, in a line, and each goal’s chart and History say “Definition changed, week {w}” with your reason. Their numbers and plans don’t change.
- Changing which way is better needs a reason too, names the goals whose target now lies the wrong way, and marks each goal.
- A new unit is either a new label for the same numbers (every goal’s unit changes with it) or a different scale. A different scale is a different metric: add it as a new metric and move goals to it, or retire this one.
- Fewer decimal places names the goals that show more; they keep theirs until their owners change them.
- Undo takes back the change, its marks and, for a new label, every goal’s unit, as one.

#### Retire, not delete

- A metric that has measured a goal is retired, not deleted: its goals keep their numbers and plans and say “Measured by {metric}, retired {date}”. It leaves the pickers and the library’s list (Retired metrics are listed apart), and it can be brought back at any time with Bring it back.
- Say why it is retired. Name what replaces it, in the same unit, and its goals’ owners are offered it on the goal’s page.
- A metric no goal has ever used is deleted instead, and can be put back from Recently removed for 30 days.

#### Merge (admins)

- An admin merges a metric into another in the same unit: every goal it measures moves to the other, keeping its For and part, and it is retired pointing there. One Undo puts it all back.

### Teams

`teams`. The workspace’s teams, A to Z, each with its lead, its people and its goals by status; a team’s page says what it is here to do. Admins add, change and remove teams.

Routes: `/teams`, `/teams/:teamId`, `/workspace/teams`. Requirements: `PEOPLE-DIRECTORY`, `WORKSPACE-ADMIN`.

#### How to use it

- Teams is the second tab of People. Find a team by its name or its lead’s.
- Each row shows the team’s lead, or No lead (set-up doesn’t ask who leads a team), how many people are in it (its lead counts as one of them, even when their own team is another), and its goals this year counted by status, shape and word. The counts are the same numbers Goals shows by team.
- Open a team to see what it is here to do, its goals by status (each count opens those goals), and its people, lead first. See its goals opens Goals for just that team; Show all lists all its people in People.

#### For admins

- Add a team is the main action. On a team’s page, Change its name, lead or purpose; and, apart, Remove this team. An empty team goes at once; a team with people or goals first moves them to another team, in the same save, and each goal’s history says so.

#### Who can

Everyone sees the teams. Only admins change them.

#### Moved

Teams used to be a section of Workspace. Its old address, /workspace/teams, still opens it, and an old link to one team’s people opens that team.

### Workspace: Cycles

`workspace-cycles`. The workspace’s goal years, newest first, with their dates, which one is running and the wrap-up; admins can delete one nobody has checked in to yet.

Routes: `/workspace/cycles`. Requirements: `UNDO-REMOVE`, `RESULTS`.

#### How to use it

- Each cycle says where it stands in a word (running; ending, in its wrap-up weeks; ended, with its last day; or starts on a date), then its week and dates (the running one) or its dates and weeks, then how many goals and check-ins it has (“no check-ins yet” for none).
- A cycle’s dates are its real first and last days: week 1’s Monday to its last week’s Sunday. The demo’s 2026 runs from 29 Dec 2025 to 3 Jan 2027.
- The current cycle also says when its wrap-up opens: the first day of its last two weeks. Once it is open, it says how many goals are still to wrap up; once the year has ended, the day it ended and until when the wrap-up stays open.
- Its one action: See the wrap-up, before it opens (once any goal has a check-in); Wrap it up, once it’s open; and for admins, once every goal is wrapped up, Start the next cycle.
- An admin can delete a cycle nobody has checked in to, with its goals: Delete… asks first (“Delete 2027 and its 4 goals? Nobody has checked in to it.”). It’s listed in Recently removed and can be restored for 30 days. One with check-ins stays, and the only cycle always stays.
- A new cycle starts from the wrap-up at the end of this one, where each goal is carried on or stopped.

#### Who can

Everyone reads Cycles and opens the wrap-up. Only admins delete a cycle or start the next one.

### Workspace: Access

`workspace-access`. For admins: who the admins are, and MCP access: the MCP tokens Claude or another AI tool uses to act as someone in this workspace.

Routes: `/workspace/access`. Requirements: `ADMIN`, `MCP-TOKENS`.

#### How to use it

- Admins lists everyone who is one, A to Z. Add an admin is the page’s main action: find someone by name, job title or team, then Make them an admin. The message that says so has Undo.
- Remove as admin, on anyone’s row, asks first (“They keep their goals and history”); on your own row it’s Stop being an admin, which has no Undo: only another admin can make you one again. There is always at least one admin: the only one has no button, and their row says The only admin.
- The same two are on a person’s page in People, under For admins, with Make an MCP token for that person.
- MCP tokens: Make a token for someone (it’s shown once), and revoke any token. The AI tool using it then acts as that person, with their rights, and every change it makes says “via MCP”. A token made as a builder token, before the inbox opened to everyone, is labelled “builder token”: it works as an ordinary one. See MCP access.
- In the demo, MCP tokens don’t work: its data stays in your browser, where an AI tool can’t reach it. Access says so in place of the list.

#### Who can

Admins. Everyone finds their own MCP tokens in Settings.

### Settings

`settings`. About you: who you are here and your page, your own choices (light or dark, an accent colour, the sidebar, how a goal’s page moves), your MCP tokens, whether recording is on, and leaving the workspace.

Routes: `/settings`. Screens: `Settings`. Requirements: `SETTINGS`, `MOTION`, `MOTION-ALIVE`, `BRAND`, `LEAVE-WORKSPACE`.

#### How to use it

- Light or dark: light, dark, or follow your device.
- Accent colour: Faro’s teal (the default), or the earlier cobalt, violet, petrol or graphite. Each is readable in light and dark. Status colours never change.
- Motion lab, at the bottom: play with how a goal’s page moves. It is off by default, so a goal’s page shows its chart and number the moment it opens; switch on “Play the story when a goal’s page opens” to watch the chart draw itself in and the number land. Then speed and impact sliders, a landing style (thump, spring, wobble or drop), switches for each effect, an optional “tock” and phone buzz when it lands, and a preview.
- Sidebar: full, or icons only. The toggle at the foot of the sidebar does the same; every icon is named on hover.
- You, first: your name, job title, team and whether you’re an admin or a member here, with Your page (your page in People). An admin changes your name, job title or team; Settings names the admins.
- Recording: one line, whether it’s on here, leading to Workspace, Privacy for what is and isn’t recorded.
- Your MCP tokens: the tokens that act as you, which you can revoke. An admin makes them, on Workspace, Access or from your page.
- Under the title, links to each part of Settings (You, Appearance, Navigation, Your MCP tokens, Leave) stay at the top as you scroll, with the part you’re in lit.
- Settings is a place of its own, so it has no back link: the menu takes you anywhere from here.
- Leave, at the very end: leave the workspace that’s open. Someone takes over your goals and open asks first, and your history stays; an admin can bring you back for 30 days. The only admin can’t leave until someone else is an admin, and is told so.

#### Good to know

How the app looks is kept in this browser only. On another device, choose again. Everyday motion is quick and subtle; a goal’s page moves at the pace you choose. All of it switches off when your device asks for reduced motion.

#### Faro’s look

The app is called Faro, the Spanish and Italian word for a lighthouse. Its logo is at the top of the sidebar (the F alone when the sidebar is icons only), at the top left on a phone, on the welcome page and in the browser tab. The workspace you’re in is named beside it (under it in the sidebar); where you choose between workspaces, each is listed by its name.

Its look is warm paper, dark ink and the lighthouse’s teal. The logo’s amber beam is used nowhere else, because in the app amber means At risk.

On a phone’s home screen and in the browser tab, the F sits on a deep-teal tile so it’s easy to spot. See On a phone, a tablet or a big screen for adding it to your home screen.

### Features: switching parts of Faro on or off

`features`. Faro is a core (people, teams, goals, plans, check-ins and the status rules) plus parts an admin can switch on or off for a workspace: how you work (Reviews) and tools such as the Metric library and Spreadsheets.

Routes: `/workspace/features`. Requirements: `MODULES`, `REVIEWS-OPTIONAL`.

#### How to use it

- On Workspace, Features says how this workspace works and lists the optional parts of Faro, each with what it does; About says which are on, from the same list. Goals, check-ins and people are the core and always on.
- How you work holds Reviews: walking a set of goals together on a cadence. While it is on, it says how many reviews are set up. Tools holds the rest, such as the Metric library and Spreadsheets. Each has a switch with On or Off beside it.
- Switching Reviews off asks first. It says, for everyone here, that Reviews leaves the menu and Home, how many reviews stay in the record with what was said in them, how many open next steps and questions raised in a review stay open, and that nothing is deleted. Cancel changes nothing; Switch off Reviews does it. Switching a tool off, or anything on, acts at once.
- Switched off, a feature leaves every screen: its pages (an old link says it is switched off, and who can switch it on), its menus and buttons, its Help and its MCP tools. Anything that needs it goes off with it, and Features says so.
- With Reviews off, asks and next steps stay on their goals and on Home, each goal’s History and Activity keep what was said in reviews, and check-ins are still due by the same day.
- Nothing a feature saved is deleted. Switch it back on and everything is as it was: every review, its people, its cadence and what was said. A session whose date passed while Reviews was off isn’t said to be not held.
- Each switch says what it did, with Undo for 10 seconds, and is logged in Activity, with who did it.
- Spreadsheets is one of the tools: Export and Import on Data, the template and Export these goals on Goals. Set-up keeps its own upload whatever the switch says.

#### Who can

Admins switch features. Everyone sees what is on.

#### For the people building Faro

- Each feature is a module: one folder in src/modules with a module.json saying what it adds and what it needs. docs/architecture.md explains how to add one.

### What the app records

`recording`. The app records how it is used, never what you type, so the people building it can see what is slow, broken or hard to use.

Routes: `/workspace/privacy`. Requirements: `TELEMETRY-SIGNALS`, `TELEMETRY-PRIVACY`, `TELEMETRY-FLOWS`, `TELEMETRY-RETENTION`, `TELEMETRY-SWITCH`.

#### What is recorded

- The pages you open, and how long each takes to show.
- The buttons you press that do something, such as posting a check-in, saving a goal or answering a request, and whether it worked.
- How far you get in a task: a check-in, a new goal, changing a goal, a review, answering a request, an import, the wrap-up or setting up a workspace. Where you start, each step you reach, and whether you finish or stop.
- Errors, saves that didn’t go through (and whether a rule said no or the connection failed), and how long loading took.
- With each: an id for this browser tab, your id in the workspace and the workspace’s id. Not your name.

#### What is never recorded

- Anything you type: notes, numbers, names, goal titles, comments, answers or searches.
- What a page shows you.
- The app only sends things it names itself, from a fixed list. Anything else is dropped in your browser before it is sent.

#### How long, and who can see it

- Each record is kept for 90 days. After that only daily totals are kept: how many, how many failed, how long they took and where people stopped, with nothing about any one visit.
- Only the people who build and run the app, and the AI that helps them, can read it. No one in your workspace can, admins included.
- It is kept in the app’s own database, in a standard format (OpenTelemetry), so it could later go to your company’s own monitoring tool.

#### When you send a markup

- A markup is sent only when you press Send. It carries the picture of your screen as it was (nothing on it is hidden, and you see it before sending), your marks, your line, your name, the page, your screen size, light or dark, your accent and the app’s version.
- It also carries your last 20 steps on this visit (the pages you opened and the buttons you pressed, never what you typed) unless you untick them, and any errors or saves that didn’t go through on this visit.
- Only the people building Faro read markups.

#### Turning it off

- A workspace records only if whoever set it up chose it: set-up asks, and it is off unless ticked. The example in the demo records. Settings says in one line whether it is on where you are, and leads to Privacy.
- Anyone can read what is recorded, and whether it is on (On or Off, in a word), on Workspace, under Privacy. Only an admin can turn it on or off there, for the whole workspace; turning it on asks first, and turning it off says so with Undo. While it is off, nothing is recorded or sent from that workspace, by the app or through MCP.

### MCP access

`ai-assistants`. Connect Claude or another AI tool to Faro through MCP with a personal MCP token, so it can read and do everything you can in the app, as you. Faro has no AI of its own: this is the door other AI tools use.

Requirements: `MCP-TOKENS`, `MCP-PARITY`, `TOKENS-SERVER-ONLY`.

#### What it can do

- Read every screen: what needs you, goals, a goal in full, requests, reviews, watching, people, activity, views, the wrap-up, this guide and what’s new.
- Do what you can: check in, set up and change goals and plans, answer requests, take part in reviews, watch goals, save views, and (as an admin) manage people and teams and turn recording on or off.
- Look after the metric library: list and read the metrics goals are measured by, add one or change one you own, and say which metric measures one of your goals, for a team or the whole company and optionally one part of it (it asks before two goals share one number, and asks why when a goal with check-ins is measured differently).
- It meets the same rules as you, with exactly your rights, and every change is logged as you, marked “via MCP”. A goal it can’t save comes back as “Not saved. Must fix:” with each problem in the words New goal uses. A goal that raises a question (over 100%, no unit, a link to a lower level, a plan that flips which way is better) comes back as “Not saved. Check with the person first:” with every question; it saves once you have said yes to each and it calls again with “confirm”.
- In one bulk change it can add a whole tree of goals and their first numbers: each new goal’s row has a Ref, and the rows below name it in Feeds into ref or Goal ref. One dry run checks it all.
- Adding goals, one at a time or many at once, it is told each new goal’s key (G-12) and ID straight away, so it can link, check in on or change them without searching first. The key is the one the goal holds once saved, even when someone else adds a goal at the same moment. A dry run says the keys the goals would get, and no IDs yet.
- Finding goals, it gets 50 at a time, with how many match in all and how to ask for the next page.
- Lists (goals it finds, asks, reviews, people, activity, views, metrics and the rest) always come back in one shape, filtered or not, so it reads them the same way every time.
- Ask it to describe the system and it gets Faro’s own overview: what the app is, how its rules work, and where its spec says the rest.
- Ask for “my goals”, “my team’s goals” or “what I’m watching” and it finds exactly what the Goals tabs Mine, My team and Watching show you.
- Paste a Goals link and it finds the same goals the link shows, its tab (Mine, My team, Watching) included.

#### How to connect

- An admin makes a personal MCP token for you under Workspace, Access, MCP access. The database makes it, keeps only a hash of it, and shows it once; nobody can read tokens back, not even through the app.
- Add the server to your AI tool with the address and token shown. For Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http goals https://<app>/api/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer gk_…".
- See and revoke your MCP tokens in Settings. The full list of tools is in docs/mcp.md.

#### Who can

Only admins make MCP tokens. An admin or the token’s own person can revoke one. Any MCP token, a builder token made before included, also reads and triages the inbox’s markups and feedback, pictures included (Connect Claude, at the top of the inbox, has the set-up).

### Send feedback, and marking up a screen

`feedback`. Tell the people building Faro what should change: mark up the screen you’re on, or say in a few words how the app is working for you.

Requirements: `MARKUP`, `FEEDBACK-RAISED`.

#### How to use it

- Go to Feedback (in the menu’s last group, or in More on a phone) and choose Send feedback. Its first choice is Mark up the last screen: it takes you back to the page you came from and keeps a picture of it. On a computer, Ctrl+Shift+M (Cmd+Shift+M on a Mac) marks up the screen you’re on from anywhere.
- The screen you’re on is kept as a still picture, and a slim toolbar appears. Draw on the picture with the Pen, an Arrow or a Box, or put down a numbered Note with a few words. Undo takes back the last mark, Clear removes them all, and Cancel (or Escape) stops without sending anything.
- Next asks one thing: what should change. You can also say how the app is working for you. It shows the exact picture that will be sent, with your marks. Go Back to change it, or Cancel.
- Send. “Sent. You’ll hear when it’s fixed.” When a release fixes it, its entry in What’s new says “You raised this”.
- Or skip the picture: choose how it’s working and add a few words, as before. It goes to the same inbox as markups, where the people building Faro mark it in hand, fixed or won’t fix. When a release fixes it, its entry in What’s new says “You raised this” too.

#### With the keyboard

- Tab to the drawing area. The arrow keys move a crosshair (with Shift, further), Enter starts and ends a mark, and P, A, B and N choose Pen, Arrow, Box and Note.
- Ctrl+Z takes back the last mark. Escape stops the mark you’re making, or else cancels.

#### What’s sent

- The picture of your screen, as it was. Nothing on it is hidden, so check it before you send.
- Your marks, your line, your name, which parts of the screen your marks are on (for example Goal page, Scorecard, Will it hit), the page, your screen size, light or dark, your accent and the app’s version.
- Your last 20 steps on this visit, unless you untick them: the pages you opened and the buttons you pressed, never what you typed. And any errors or saves that didn’t go through on this visit.
- In the demo, markups are sent too, marked as from the demo. Anyone can read them in the inbox on Workspace, picture included: Faro holds no real data, so nothing on your screen should be private.

### The inbox

`inbox`. Every markup and piece of feedback people send, from every workspace and the demo, on its own page, Feedback, beside Help. Open to anyone with no sign-in: work through it like an inbox, from New to In hand to Closed.

Routes: `/feedback`, `/workspace/inbox`, `/inbox`. Screens: `Feedback`. Requirements: `MARKUP-INBOX`, `FEEDBACK-INBOX`, `MCP-FEEDBACK`, `CONNECT-CLAUDE`, `MCP-PICTURES`, `INBOX-TRIAGE`, `FEEDBACK-PAGE`.

#### Who can read it

- The inbox is its own page, Feedback, beside Help in the sidebar (in More on a phone), in the app and the demo. It was a section of Workspace; it moved because it belongs to no one workspace. Old links to Workspace’s inbox open it.
- It holds what’s sent from every workspace and the demo, and says where each came from. There’s no sign-in: anyone can read it and send feedback, on any device. Only an admin changes a status (In hand, Fixed, Won’t fix, New again); everyone else sees a line saying so, and no buttons. Every change says who made it and can be undone. Faro holds no real data, so there is nothing to keep back. The company’s own app keeps its inbox to the people who look after the app.
- It names people, never their email. The New tab says how many are new; The New tab counts them across every workspace.
- Send feedback, at the top, opens the feedback sheet; it says which page you came from, and Mark up the last screen goes back to it.

#### Working through it

- Three tabs: New, In hand and Closed (fixed or won’t fix), each with how many it holds. When New is empty, it says Nothing new.
- Each row starts with its status as a shape and a word, then what was said, the part of the page it’s about (or, for feedback, its mood and page), who sent it, from where and when.
